newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-GRAF GONE BUT HINGIS HOLDS ON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF GONE BUT HINGIS HOLDS ON.

text.p: Top seed Martina Hingis breezed past former champion Aranxta Sanchez Vicario at the French Open on Tuesday, setting the scene for a semifinal clash with three-times winner Monica Seles.

In a tournament of wildly inconsistent results, including the unexpected departure of second seed Steffi Graf earlier in the day, the Swiss teenager has remained the sole constant, extending her unbeaten record this season to 36 matches with a 6-2 6-2 dismantling of the sixth-seeded Spaniard in just 64 minutes.
The Australian Open champion, sidelined for a month leading up to the grand slam event after injuring her knee in a horse riding fall, could have expected a much sterner test from Sanchez Vicario.
The Spaniard is renowned for her tenaciousness and traditionally saves her best tennis for Roland Garros, where she has twice won the tournament.
But this time Sanchez Vicario appeared helpless against the 16-year-old Swiss, who moved her around the court at will and confounded her with a wide array of shots.
"It wasn't easy," Hingis said. "At the beginning she was playing really well, hitting the ball really hard.
"After I lost the first game I thought, either I start playing or go home. After that I started hitting everything in, I started playing an unbelievable game -- I couldn't believe it."
The victory set up a much anticipated showdown with Seles, who outlasted compatriot Mary Joe Fernandez 3-6 6-2 7-5 in an all-U.S. quarter-final clash to become the last remaining American in Paris.
It will be the third time this year the two will have clashed, adding fuel to what is rapidly turning into an intense rivalry.

"I don't have a great track record against her lately," said Seles, who lost to Hingis in the finals of the Lipton and Hilton Head. "She's playing great tennis right now and beat Arantxa very quickly.
"She hasn't lost yet this year and I think that says it all.
"I'm not going to think about those past results, I'm just going to think about the present."
The other semifinal pits South Africa's Amanda Coetzer against Croatia's Iva Majoli.
Coetzer earned her place in the final four by ending Graf's grand slam title hopes for the second time this year.

World number two Graf, who had reached the final at Roland Garros eight times in the last 10 years, was swept aside 6-1 6-4 by the opponent who humiliated her 6-0 6-1 in Berlin last month and dispatched her from the Australian Open in January.
"I could sense she lacked confidence," Coetzer said. "But I can understand that.
"She's been injured and hasn't played much and I've had a couple of wins over her, so I know I would feel the same way."

Having missed three months of tennis earlier this year with tendinitis in her left knee, Graf was in trouble right from her opening serve as Coetzer broke her twice in the first set to jump out to a 4-0 lead.

Graf, winner of the last two French Opens, did her best to stage a comeback following a 30-minute rain delay in the second set but ultimately slid to her first defeat in Paris since losing in the 1994 semifinals to Mary Pierce.
"It was a difficult match, I was really nervous and made a lot of mistakes," Graf, five times French Open champion, said.
"It's just the state I'm in, I just don't seem to have the confidence against her. I've struggled in all my matches here but I was always able to turn them around. That wasn't the case today."
Coetzer will meet Iva Majoli in the semifinals and Graf, for one, does not fancy the diminutive South African's chances of advancing to the final over her 19-year-old Croatian opponent.
"Probably not," said Graf when asked if she expected to see Coetzer in Saturday's final. "She's playing with confidence and steady but to win the tournament would be difficult for her."

Majoli, the ninth seed, earned her first appearance in a grand slam semifinal after struggling to a 6-3 5-7 6-2 win over her doubles partner Ruxandra Dragomir in a gruelling match which took two hours and 23 minutes to complete.
